Site.title: jsrosetta — Node.js to Go, Rust, Swift, Java
Site.description: Translate Node.js/JavaScript syntax into Go, Rust, Swift and Java. One concept per post, compared side by side across languages.

Home.heading: Write Node.js? Read every other language.
Home.intro: Each post takes a familiar JavaScript concept and sets it next to the equivalent code in other languages. Pick a language in any code block and the whole page follows.

Lang.title: Node.js → {label}
Lang.description: Every Node.js/JavaScript concept alongside its equivalent in {label}.
Lang.count: {count, plural, one {# concept} other {# concepts}} with {label} examples.

intro.go: Go is a compiled, statically typed language that handles concurrency with goroutines and channels instead of Node.js's event loop. Each post below puts a JavaScript concept next to its Go equivalent, along with the differences that trip people up, such as errors returned as values and slices in place of arrays.
intro.rust: Rust manages memory with ownership and the borrow checker instead of a garbage collector, and models errors and missing values with Result and Option. Each post below puts a JavaScript concept next to its Rust equivalent so you can see what carries over and what needs a different mindset.
intro.swift: Swift is statically typed, uses optionals instead of null/undefined, treats structs as value types and supports async/await with structured concurrency. Each post below puts a JavaScript concept next to its Swift equivalent, with a note wherever an API is Apple-only.
intro.java: Modern Java has records, the Stream API, pattern matching and virtual threads, and is far leaner than its old reputation. Each post below puts a JavaScript concept next to its Java equivalent, along with the differences in static typing, exceptions and concurrency.
